newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares a tad weaker, OTC takes breather.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares a tad weaker, OTC takes breather.

text.p: Singapore shares opened a shade softer on Tuesday while Malaysian counters took a breather from recent rallies, dealers said.

At 0215 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was off 9.35 points, at 2,223.05 while the UOB OTC index shaved off 1.98 points at 1,249.07. Total market turnover was around 47 million, with losers outnumbering gainers by 153 to 63.

Malaysian shares continued to hog the actives. Leading the pack was paper and investment firm, Insas Bhd, which saw over 3.6 million shares traded. Its shares were around Singapore $1.05 (US$0.75), up a cent.
Malaysian KLI Holdings remained among the actives, with over 3.9 million shares on reported rumours that a Hong Kong tycoon was keen on acquiring stakes in the investment company.

Some dealers said arbitraging appeared limited now that the stock price in Singapore has narrowed the gap with its Kuala Lumpur counterpart. The shares were trading at S$2.42 in SES and 4.46 ringgit in KLSE.
Foreign tranches of OUB and Singapore Press led gainers, rising S$0.30 each to S$11.20 and S$27.30 respectively. Cerebos Pacific led losers, shedding S$0.40 to S$10.80.
